header.text: This diagram shows the life cycle of an apple tree.

alternativeText.text: A circular diagram shows the life stages of an apple tree. The first stage is labeled "seedling" and shows a small green plant with three leaves sprouting from a seed. The next stage is labeled "adult tree" and shows a large tree with leaves, flowers, and apples on its branches. Next, a close-up of a single tree branch shows a flower with five petals. The center of the flower has short, thin stalks with a yellow substance labeled "pollen" on their tips. A bee is flying toward the pollen. Another close-up of the flower shows a stalk labeled "anther" and the center of the flower labeled "pistil". Now, the bee is touching the pollen. Then, a close-up of the same branch shows an apple where the flower used to be. Finally, the inside of the apple is shown with black "seeds" labeled in its center. An arrow points back to the seedling to show a complete cycle.
